html:
The Pilagá are an Indigenous people of the Gran Chaco in Formosa province, northern Argentina. They speak a Guaicuruan language close to that of the Qom, and like the Abipón they once lived by hunting, fishing and gathering across the Chaco plains.

The Argentine army took control of their lands only in the late 1800s and early 1900s. In October 1947, at Rincón Bomba near Las Lomitas, the border police massacred hundreds of Pilagá who had gathered at a religious meeting. In 2019 an Argentine court ruled the killing a crime against humanity.
